subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 0 easy / 48 medium / 52 hard. Tier is relative: the hard third of the 60 papers by average question difficulty. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: In COPD (emphysema), which lung volume is typically increased?
questions.explanation: Air trapping increases residual volume and functional residual capacity; vital capacity and FEV1 decrease.

questions.question: The anterior drawer test of the ankle stresses the:
questions.explanation: Anterior translation of the talus from the mortise indicates ATFL laxity.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the capacitor-field method of SWD the tissues are placed between two electrodes and the dominant heating effect is in tissues of:

options.B: Low impedance such as muscle only
options.D: High impedance such as fat and superficial structures

questions.explanation: In an electric field, heating is greatest in tissues with high resistance (fat, skin), so the capacitor-field method heats subcutaneous fat first; in the inductive method, high-conductivity tissue (muscle) heats more via eddy currents.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Tenodesis grasp is a functional hand strategy in complete tetraplegia at:
questions.explanation: C6 patients have wrist extensors (ECRL) but no finger flexors; active wrist extension closes the fingers passively through tendon tension, so finger flexor shortening must be avoided.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Shoulder pain and subluxation in the flaccid hemiplegic arm are best prevented by:

options.A: Supporting the arm during transfers and positioning, avoiding pulling on the arm, and using a tray or supports
options.C: Leaving the arm unsupported in dependency

questions.explanation: Do not use overhead pulleys; position the arm in lateral rotation and abduction with support; use slings only when necessary.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Approximation and joint compression increase postural tone mainly by stimulating:

options.D: Joint receptors and proprioceptors (and the antigravity extensors)

questions.explanation: Approximation (compression through the joints) facilitates co-contraction and proprioceptive input; traction inhibits.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The H-reflex is clinically used to assess conduction through:

options.A: The S1 root (via the tibial nerve to soleus)
options.C: The C5 root via musculocutaneous nerve

questions.explanation: The H-reflex is the electrical analogue of the ankle jerk: a monosynaptic reflex through the S1 segment. A delayed or absent H-reflex suggests S1 radiculopathy or neuropathy.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The External Rotation Recurvatum Test, in which the examiner lifts both of the patient's big toes off the table and observes for relative hyperextension and lateral tibial rotation on the affected side, is a test for:
questions.explanation: The External Rotation Recurvatum Test assesses for posterolateral rotary instability in extension — a positive test shows the affected knee falling into relative hyperextension (genu varum appearance) with lateral tibial rotation due to gravity, when both legs are lifted by the toes.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — External Rotation Recurvatum Test
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Pressure of an axillary crutch pad in the axilla can cause injury to the:
questions.explanation: Crutch palsy affects the radial nerve (wrist drop); weight must be borne through the hands.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The D-dimer test has high sensitivity but low specificity for pulmonary embolism. What does this mean in practice?

options.A: A positive D-dimer confirms pulmonary embolism definitively
options.B: A negative D-dimer helps rule out pulmonary embolism, but a positive result does not confirm it — it only means the disease has not been excluded
options.C: The D-dimer test is useless in clinical practice
options.D: High sensitivity and low specificity mean the test is always accurate regardless of result

questions.explanation: A highly sensitive test detects most true disease (few false negatives), so a negative result is reassuring and helps exclude the disease. But low specificity means many people without the disease will still test positive (false positives) — so a raised D-dimer does not confirm pulmonary embolism, it simply means it cannot yet be excluded, prompting further imaging.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Interpreting Test Results
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: By definition, a transient ischemic attack (TIA) produces focal neurological deficits that:

options.A: Last longer than 24 hours with permanent residual damage
options.B: Do not last longer than 24 hours, with no evidence of residual brain damage afterward
options.C: Always progress to a completed stroke within 24 hours
options.D: Only ever affect vision, never motor function

questions.explanation: A TIA is a temporary interruption of blood supply producing focal neurological deficits lasting minutes to hours but, by definition, not longer than 24 hours, with no evidence of residual damage afterward. However, TIA is clinically significant as a warning sign — about 15% of strokes are preceded by a TIA, with the highest risk in the following 90 days.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan, Physical Rehabilitation
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The dermatome of the middle finger is:
questions.explanation: C6 thumb, C7 middle, C8 little finger.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Prolonged immobilisation commonly results in all EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Immobility causes disuse osteopenia, contracture, hypercalciuria with stones, pressure sores and DVT; gallstones are not an effect.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The main blood supply to the head of the femur in adults is through the:

options.C: Retinacular branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery
options.D: Artery of the ligamentum teres only

questions.explanation: Intracapsular fractures disrupt this supply — risk of avascular necrosis.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The Gibbs-Donnan membrane equilibrium describes what happens when a membrane permeable to some ions separates two solutions, one of which also contains a non-diffusible (non-penetrating) ion such as a protein anion. What is the key consequence?

options.A: All ions distribute exactly equally on both sides regardless of the non-diffusible ion
options.B: The diffusible ions distribute asymmetrically at equilibrium — the diffusible cation concentration is higher on the side containing the non-penetrating anion
options.C: The non-diffusible ion eventually crosses the membrane too, given enough time
options.D: No electrical potential difference develops across the membrane

questions.explanation: When a non-diffusible anion (like a protein) is confined to one side, the freely diffusible ions (like K+ and Cl-) redistribute asymmetrically at equilibrium to maintain electrical neutrality and equal ion products on both sides — the diffusible cation ends up more concentrated on the side with the trapped anion. This asymmetry is the Gibbs-Donnan equilibrium and contributes to the resting membrane potential.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.sourceChapter: The Membrane Potentials — Gibbs-Donnan Membrane Equilibrium
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: The lumbar facet joints are oriented mainly in the:

options.A: Sagittal plane, allowing flexion/extension and limiting rotation

questions.explanation: Cervical facets lie at ~45°, thoracic in the coronal plane (rotation and lateral flexion), lumbar in the sagittal plane.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A grade I acromioclavicular sprain presents with:

options.B: Gross upward displacement of the clavicle
options.C: Complete rupture of the coracoclavicular ligaments
options.D: Local tenderness and mild pain, with no visible deformity and normal stability

questions.explanation: Grade I: AC ligament sprain only. Grade II: AC torn, CC sprained. Grade III: both torn with visible step deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: When a muscle is immobilized after injury, which muscle fiber type atrophies at a FASTER rate, and what is the clinical implication?

options.A: Type II (fast twitch) fibers atrophy faster, so power training should be prioritized immediately
options.B: Type I (slow twitch) fibers atrophy faster, contributing to faster atrophy of antigravity muscles and underscoring the need for early endurance training
options.C: Both fiber types atrophy at exactly the same rate with immobilization
options.D: Immobilization has no effect on muscle fiber composition

questions.explanation: With immobilization, Type I (slow twitch) fibers atrophy faster than Type II (fast twitch) fibers, and there is also a slow-to-fast fiber type conversion with disuse. Since antigravity (postural) muscles rely heavily on Type I fibers, this contributes to their faster rate of atrophy compared to their antagonists — supporting early initiation of endurance-type training after injury or surgery.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 6: Resistance Exercise — Muscle Fiber Atrophy
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: 'Rusty' coloured sputum is classically associated with infection by which organism?
questions.explanation: Rusty-coloured sputum is a classic finding associated with pneumococcal infection (typical lobar pneumonia), whereas dark green/brown sputum suggests Pseudomonas, and 'red-currant jelly' sputum suggests Klebsiella.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: To produce measurable separation of lumbar vertebrae, the traction force needs to exceed approximately:
questions.explanation: Because of the friction of the body on the couch and the strength of the lumbar ligaments, forces of roughly 50% of body weight or more are needed for lumbar separation; lower forces (about 25%) are used for comfort and initial treatment.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Among the TORCH agents, which one is most harmful to the fetus specifically when acquired during the first 10 weeks of pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Rubella (German measles) is teratogenic, and infection during the acute stage of the first 10 weeks of pregnancy is far more harmful to the fetus than infection later in gestation, producing the classic congenital rubella syndrome (ocular defects, cardiac defects, CNS manifestations, sensorineural deafness).
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.sourceChapter: Infectious and Parasitic Diseases — TORCH Complex
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Stability of a body is increased by:

options.C: Moving the line of gravity to the edge of the base
options.D: Widening the base of support and lowering the centre of gravity

questions.explanation: A wide base and low centre of mass require a greater force to tip the body.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: True leg length is measured from the:

options.B: Anterior superior iliac spine to the medial malleolus
options.C: Greater trochanter to the lateral malleolus

questions.explanation: True length: ASIS to medial malleolus; apparent length: umbilicus (or xiphisternum) to the medial malleolus.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Rabies is transmitted mainly by:

options.C: The bite of an infected dog, with saliva containing the virus

questions.explanation: Hydrophobia; 100% fatal once symptoms appear; post-exposure prophylaxis is vital.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Per the criteria described for a 'normal pregnancy', delivery is expected to occur at term (between 38-42 weeks) with a fetal weight of at least:

options.D: Weight is not part of the criteria

questions.explanation: The criteria for a 'normal pregnancy' include delivery of a single baby in good condition at term (38-42 weeks), with a fetal weight of 2.5 kg or more, and with no maternal complications — making 'normal pregnancy' technically a retrospective classification.
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Cryotherapy is used to temporarily reduce spasticity because it:

options.B: Lowers nerve conduction velocity and muscle spindle firing

questions.explanation: Cooling decreases afferent firing and conduction velocity, lowering tone for a short period during which stretching or exercise can be performed.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Normal chest expansion measured at the level of the nipples is approximately:
questions.explanation: Normal chest expansion ≥5 cm; reduced in ankylosing spondylitis (<2.5 cm).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A confounding factor is one that:

options.B: Lies on the causal pathway only
options.C: Is not associated with the outcome
options.D: Is associated with both the exposure and the outcome and distorts their observed relationship

questions.explanation: Control by randomisation, restriction, matching or adjustment.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Resisted isometric movement that is strong and painful suggests a lesion of:
questions.explanation: Cyriax: pain on resisted testing with full passive range indicates a contractile lesion; painful passive and active movement (non-contractile) suggests an inert structure.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The acute inflammatory stage of soft tissue healing typically lasts approximately how long, unless the insult is perpetuated?
questions.explanation: The acute inflammatory stage typically lasts 4 to 6 days unless the injury is continually aggravated. The subsequent subacute (proliferation/repair) stage usually lasts 10-17 days (up to 6 weeks in poorly vascularised tissues like tendons), and the chronic (maturation/remodeling) stage can last 6 months to 1 year.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 10: Soft Tissue Injury, Repair, and Management — Acute Stage
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Bile salts are essential for:
questions.explanation: Cholecystokinin causes gallbladder contraction.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes tendinitis, tenosynovitis, and tendinosis?

options.A: Tendinitis is inflammation of a tendon; tenosynovitis is inflammation of the synovial membrane covering a tendon; tendinosis is degeneration of the tendon from repetitive microtrauma (not primarily inflammatory)
options.B: All three terms describe exactly the same pathological process
options.C: Tendinosis is an acute inflammatory condition, more severe than tendinitis
options.D: Tenosynovitis only affects ligaments, never tendons

questions.explanation: Tendinitis is inflammation of a tendon (possibly with scarring or calcium deposits); tenosynovitis is inflammation of the synovial membrane covering a tendon; tendinosis is tendon degeneration from repetitive microtrauma, distinct from the acute inflammatory conditions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 10: Soft Tissue Injury, Repair, and Management — Soft Tissue Lesions
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A type I error occurs when:

options.B: A true null hypothesis is rejected (false positive)
options.D: A false null hypothesis is accepted

questions.explanation: Alpha is the probability of a type I error; type II (beta) is a false negative; power = 1 − beta.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis, inhibited by statins, is:
questions.explanation: Statins reduce LDL cholesterol; a side effect is myopathy.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: In a normal walking cycle the stance phase occupies about:
questions.explanation: Stance ≈60% (with double support ≈20%) and swing ≈40%. Running has no double support.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.topic: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle
questions.question: Because of accommodation, which type of current change is MORE effective at initiating a nerve impulse: a sudden change, or a gradual one?

options.A: A sudden change in current is more effective than a gradual one
options.B: A gradual change is always more effective
options.C: Both are exactly equally effective in all cases
options.D: Neither a sudden nor gradual change can ever initiate an impulse

questions.explanation: Because the nerve accommodates (adapts) to slowly changing conditions, a current that rises or falls suddenly is more effective at initiating an impulse than one that changes gradually, since gradual change gives the nerve time to accommodate before the threshold is reached.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy
questions.sourceChapter: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle — Accommodation
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The characteristic lesion of rheumatic carditis is the:
questions.explanation: Aschoff bodies contain Anitschkow cells (caterpillar cells).
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Which neurotransmitter system is most strongly implicated in the GABA-benzodiazepine receptor theory of anxiety, given that drugs facilitating its transmission relieve anxiety while antagonists provoke it?
questions.explanation: GABA is the most prevalent inhibitory neurotransmitter in the CNS. Benzodiazepines facilitate GABA transmission and relieve anxiety, while benzodiazepine antagonists (e.g. flumazenil) and inverse agonists (e.g. beta-carbolines) provoke anxiety — strong evidence linking altered GABA function to the biological basis of anxiety disorders.
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.sourceChapter: Neurotic, Stress-related and Somatoform Disorders — Anxiety Disorder, Aetiology
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: In an adult the spinal cord ends (conus medullaris) at the level of:
questions.explanation: Lumbar puncture is done at L3–L4 or L4–L5.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Myasthenia gravis is caused by:

options.C: Autoantibodies against postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction

questions.explanation: Muscle weakness worsens with activity and improves with rest; treated with anticholinesterases such as pyridostigmine.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In the Salter–Harris classification, a type II injury involves:

options.B: A fracture through the physis only
options.C: A fracture into the epiphysis only
options.D: A fracture through the physis extending into the metaphysis

questions.explanation: Type I: physis; II: physis + metaphysis (commonest); III: physis + epiphysis; IV: through all three; V: crush.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Which lamp is the best choice to irradiate a small, localised area such as a sinus or a cavity?

options.C: A water-cooled Kromayer lamp with a quartz applicator

questions.explanation: The Kromayer lamp is a water-cooled mercury vapour lamp whose UV is directed through a quartz applicator in contact with the tissue, allowing treatment of sinuses, cavities and small ulcers.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The Hill–Sachs lesion occurs on the:

options.A: Anteromedial aspect of the humeral head
options.C: Posterolateral aspect of the humeral head

questions.explanation: It is an impaction fracture of the posterolateral humeral head against the anterior glenoid rim during anterior dislocation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Addison's disease is characterised by:
questions.explanation: Adrenal cortical insufficiency; treat with hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: In a child presenting with acute scrotal pain, testicular torsion must be relieved within approximately what time window from symptom onset for a good chance of testicular salvage?
questions.explanation: Testicular torsion must be relieved within 6-8 hours of symptom onset for a good chance of salvaging the testis — this is why any acute scrotum where torsion cannot be confidently excluded requires urgent surgical exploration.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Paediatric Surgery — The Acute Scrotum
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: A pulsed ultrasound output with a duty cycle of 20% corresponds to a mark : space ratio of:
questions.explanation: Duty cycle = on time / (on + off) = 1/(1+4) = 20%. A 1:1 ratio is a 50% duty cycle.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A ‘benchmark disability’ under the RPwD Act 2016 refers to:

options.A: A person with at least 40% of a specified disability

questions.explanation: People with benchmark disability are eligible for government benefits.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Phonophoresis is the use of ultrasound to:

options.A: Reduce skin resistance to direct current
options.B: Drive a topical drug through the skin into underlying tissue
options.C: Remove a drug from the blood

questions.explanation: Phonophoresis uses acoustic streaming and increased membrane permeability to deliver topical agents such as hydrocortisone or NSAIDs.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: During the loading response of walking, the vertical ground reaction force peaks at about:
questions.explanation: Vertical GRF shows a double hump: first at weight acceptance, a dip at mid-stance (~80%) and second peak at push-off.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Exclusive breastfeeding provides approximately what level of contraceptive protection for the first 6 months postpartum?
questions.explanation: In a woman who is exclusively breastfeeding, lactational amenorrhoea provides approximately 98% contraceptive protection for up to 6 months postpartum — a recognised natural method of contraception, though ovulation can occasionally precede the return of menstruation.
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: The normal range of ankle dorsiflexion is about:
questions.explanation: AAOS: ankle dorsiflexion 0–20°, plantar flexion 0–50°, inversion 0–35°, eversion 0–15°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The alternating vasoconstriction and vasodilatation that occurs in the skin when cold is applied for a prolonged period is called:
questions.explanation: Prolonged cold causes cold-induced vasodilatation every few minutes to protect tissue from freezing; this limits the benefit of very long applications.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In manual muscle testing, the 'break test' is best described as:

options.A: Applying resistance throughout an actively moving joint to see when motion ceases
options.B: Bringing the part to the end of its available range and asking the patient to hold that position while the therapist tries to force ('break') it out of position
options.C: Passively moving a joint until tissue resistance is felt
options.D: Timing how long a muscle can sustain a maximal isometric hold

questions.explanation: The break test — the most commonly used MMT procedure — has the patient hold the end-range test position while the therapist applies gradually increasing resistance, attempting to 'break' the hold. The alternative 'active resistance test' (resisting throughout the motion) requires more skill and is not generally recommended because results are often equivocal.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels and Worthingham's Muscle Testing, 9th ed.
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 1: Principles of Manual Muscle Testing
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Pyridoxal phosphate is required for the synthesis of delta-aminolevulinic acid, which is the precursor for:
questions.explanation: PLP is required for the synthesis of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA), the key precursor molecule in the heme biosynthesis pathway — linking vitamin B6 status to haemoglobin production.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: The (modified) Wells score is a clinical prediction rule used to estimate pre-test probability for which condition?
questions.explanation: The Wells score is a clinical prediction rule used to estimate the pre-test probability of pulmonary embolism (and, in another version, deep vein thrombosis), helping guide which further tests (e.g. D-dimer, CT pulmonary angiogram) are appropriate.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Clinical Prediction Rules

questions.topic: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle
questions.question: At what approximate stimulation frequency does a muscle contraction become fully tetanic, with no perceptible relaxation between successive contractions?

options.D: Frequency has no relationship to tetany

questions.explanation: As stimulation frequency increases beyond 20 Hz, partial tetany develops; further increases progressively reduce relaxation until, at frequencies over 60 Hz, there is no perceptible relaxation between contractions and the response is fully tetanic.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy
questions.sourceChapter: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle — Effects of Frequency of Stimulation
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Compared with voluntary contraction, electrically stimulated muscle contraction tends to recruit motor units:

options.A: Randomly with no relation to fibre size
options.B: In a reverse (non-selective) order, with large, fast-fatiguing units recruited first
options.C: In the same order, smallest first

questions.explanation: Large-diameter axons have the lowest electrical threshold, so large fast (type II) units are activated first; this is the reverse of the size principle and explains early fatigue with electrical stimulation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) for cerebral palsy has:

options.A: Five levels, I being the least impaired and V the most

questions.explanation: Level I walks without limitations; level V is transported in a manual wheelchair.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A 'retractile' testis is distinguished from a true undescended testis by the fact that:

options.A: A retractile testis can be manipulated without tension into the base of the scrotum, though it is pulled back up by the cremaster muscle
options.B: A retractile testis is always impalpable
options.C: A retractile testis requires orchidopexy immediately
options.D: There is no meaningful difference between the two

questions.explanation: A retractile testis can be brought down to the base of the scrotum without tension, but is then pulled back up by an overactive cremaster reflex — over time it usually resides permanently in the scrotum, though follow-up is still advised as it can rarely re-ascend and require orchidopexy.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Paediatric Surgery — Undescended Testes
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Oral polio vaccine is best stored at the primary vaccine store at:
questions.explanation: OPV is stored in the freezer at the district store; it can be kept at +2 to +8 °C for limited periods.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Complex decongestive therapy for lymphoedema includes:

options.D: Manual lymphatic drainage, compression bandaging, exercise and skin care

questions.explanation: CDT has an intensive phase and a maintenance phase; avoid heat and trauma to the limb.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Warfarin therapy is monitored by the:
questions.explanation: APTT monitors unfractionated heparin; target INR is usually 2–3.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts

questions.question: In the standard manual muscle test for the gluteus medius the patient lies:

options.A: Supine with the hip flexed to 90°
options.C: On the side with the test leg uppermost, abducting in slight extension and lateral rotation neutral
options.D: Prone with the knee flexed to 90°

questions.explanation: Side-lying with the hip slightly extended and neutral rotation to avoid substitution by TFL (flexion/medial rotation) and the hip flexors.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In axonotmesis the nerve injury is characterised by:

options.B: Complete transection of the nerve trunk
options.C: Transient conduction block with no Wallerian degeneration
options.D: Axon and myelin damage with an intact endoneurial tube, allowing recovery at about 1 mm per day

questions.explanation: Seddon: neurapraxia (block only), axonotmesis (axon disruption, connective tissue intact), neurotmesis (complete disruption). Regeneration proceeds at ~1 mm/day or 1 inch per month in axonotmesis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Langhans' giant cells, with nuclei arranged in a horseshoe pattern at the periphery, are typical of:
questions.explanation: Foreign body giant cells have randomly scattered nuclei.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: In ATLS classification, a Class III haemorrhage involves loss of:
questions.explanation: Class I <15%, II 15–30%, III 30–40% (hypotension, tachycardia >120), IV >40%.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In PNF, the technique that uses an isometric contraction of the antagonist (tight) muscle followed by relaxation and passive movement into increased range is:
questions.explanation: Hold–relax and contract–relax technique improve range by autogenic inhibition; agonist contraction techniques use reciprocal inhibition.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In correcting clubfoot by the Ponseti serial casting method, the deformity corrected FIRST is the:
questions.explanation: CAVE order: Cavus, Adductus, Varus, then Equinus last (often with a percutaneous Achilles tenotomy).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Hydrostatic pressure on a limb immersed in water helps to:

options.A: Reduce oedema and increase venous return
options.C: Decrease heart rate and venous return

questions.explanation: Pressure increases with depth and acts equally on all surfaces.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Both bones of the forearm in an adult are best immobilised in:
questions.explanation: Neutral rotation keeps the interosseous membrane tensioned and balances pronator and supinator forces.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In uncomplicated acute myocardial infarction, early mobilisation (sitting out of bed) is usually begun within:
questions.explanation: Prolonged bed rest causes deconditioning, DVT and orthostatic intolerance; progress with monitoring.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly and oesophageal dysmotility are features of:
questions.explanation: CREST: calcinosis, Raynaud's, oesophageal dysmotility, sclerodactyly, telangiectasia.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts

questions.question: The hallmark microscopic feature of coagulative necrosis is:

options.A: Complete liquefaction with no recognisable cell outlines
options.B: Preservation of the basic outline of the cell ('tombstones') even though cytoplasmic and nuclear detail is lost
options.C: Cheese-like, structureless material with surrounding granulomatous inflammation
options.D: Formation of calcium soaps from adipocyte breakdown

questions.explanation: In coagulative necrosis, cells are converted into 'tombstones' — their outline and cell type remain recognisable even though the cytoplasmic and nuclear details are lost; unlike liquefactive necrosis, cell digestion and liquefaction do not occur.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.sourceChapter: Cell Injury, Cellular Adaptations and Cellular Ageing — Coagulative Necrosis
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: The first heart sound (S1) is produced by closure of the:
questions.explanation: S1 ‘lub’ marks the start of ventricular systole; S2 ‘dub’ is semilunar valve closure.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: LSVT BIG is an exercise programme for Parkinson's disease that focuses on:

options.A: High-amplitude, high-effort movements to counteract hypokinesia

questions.explanation: LSVT BIG targets bradykinesia/hypokinesia by training large amplitude movements with high effort, 4 days/week for 4 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In anaphylactic shock from drug hypersensitivity, what is described as the only truly life-saving measure?
questions.explanation: Intramuscular adrenaline is the only life-saving measure in anaphylactic shock or laryngeal angioedema, repeated every 5-10 minutes if needed. Antihistamines and glucocorticoids have adjuvant value (glucocorticoids act slowly but help with prolonged/severe reactions) but are not substitutes for adrenaline.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.sourceChapter: Adverse Drug Effects — Treatment of Drug Allergy
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: Anatomical dead space in a healthy adult is approximately:
questions.explanation: Alveolar ventilation = (TV − dead space) × RR.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Klumpke's paralysis involves the:

options.D: Lower trunk (C8–T1), causing paralysis of the intrinsic hand muscles

questions.explanation: Klumpke's palsy affects C8–T1: claw hand with possible Horner's syndrome if T1 sympathetic fibres are involved.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A positive Romberg test (swaying or falling with the eyes closed) indicates loss of:
questions.explanation: Standing with feet together and eyes closed removes visual compensation; sway indicates a sensory ataxia.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the two-state receptor model (Ra = active, Ri = inactive conformation), an inverse agonist is one that:

options.A: Binds Ra and Ri with exactly equal affinity, producing no net change
options.B: Has high affinity for the Ri (inactive) state, shifting equilibrium away from Ra and producing an effect opposite to the agonist
options.C: Cannot bind the receptor at all in either state
options.D: Only functions on receptors with no baseline (constitutive) activity

questions.explanation: An inverse agonist preferentially binds and stabilizes the inactive (Ri) receptor conformation. This only produces an observable opposite effect on receptors that show constitutive activation (some baseline Ra signal even without agonist) — by pulling the equilibrium further toward Ri, it reduces signalling below the unstimulated baseline.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.sourceChapter: Mechanism of Drug Action; Receptor Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: Following bilateral removal of the hippocampus and amygdala (to control severe epilepsy), the famous patient H.M. could still learn new motor/perceptual skills (like tracing a mirror-image star) without any conscious memory of having practiced them before. This dissociation illustrates the difference between:

options.B: Procedural memory (how to do things) and declarative memory (memory of specific events)
options.D: Retrograde amnesia and anterograde amnesia only, with no other distinction

questions.explanation: H.M. retained procedural memory — he could learn and improve at tasks like mirror-tracing or the Tower of Hanoi over repeated sessions — even though he had no declarative (event) memory of ever having done the task before. This case was pivotal in showing procedural and declarative memory are at least partly separate systems.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Biology of Behavior — Temporal-Lobe Association Cortex, Memory Functions
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: The normal neck-shaft angle of the femur in the adult is approximately:
questions.explanation: Coxa vara <120°; coxa valga >135°.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: A Bankart lesion is:

options.A: A compression defect of the posterolateral humeral head
options.B: Avulsion of the anteroinferior glenoid labrum with the capsule
options.D: A tear of the long head of biceps

questions.explanation: Anterior dislocation avulses the anteroinferior labrum (Bankart); the humeral head impacts to cause a Hill–Sachs defect posterolaterally.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Functionally, the iliotibial tract's main role during standing with slightly flexed knees (e.g. leaning forward) is to:

options.A: Provide the main support of the knee against gravity, stabilizing it in extension and partial flexion
options.B: Flex the knee actively against resistance
options.C: Provide sensation to the anterior thigh only
options.D: Have no functional role in standing or walking

questions.explanation: The iliotibial tract stabilizes the knee in both extension and partial flexion, and is used constantly during walking and running. When leaning forward with slightly flexed knees, it becomes the main support of the knee against gravity.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Lower Limb
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The commonest site of colorectal carcinoma is the:
questions.explanation: Left-sided tumours cause altered bowel habit; right-sided cause anaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: In restrictive lung disease the typical pulmonary function pattern is:

options.B: Reduced FVC with a normal or increased FEV1/FVC ratio

questions.explanation: Restriction reduces all lung volumes proportionally, so the ratio stays normal or high (e.g. pulmonary fibrosis).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The main benefit of continuous passive motion (CPM) after ligament reconstruction is:

options.C: Reduction of joint stiffness and adhesion formation

questions.explanation: CPM is an adjunct that maintains mobility and nutrition of cartilage; it does not replace active exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: In a patient with raised intracranial pressure, which therapy position is generally preferred?

options.C: Head elevated about 30° with the neck in neutral

questions.explanation: Head-up 30° facilitates venous drainage; avoid hip flexion >90°, Valsalva and neck constriction.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Exercise should be terminated if a cardiac patient develops:

options.C: A heart rate rise of 20 bpm
options.D: Chest pain, marked dyspnoea, dizziness or a drop in systolic BP with exercise

questions.explanation: Warning signs: angina, severe breathlessness, pallor, dizziness, arrhythmias, ST depression >2 mm, hypotensive response.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The dose (energy density) delivered in laser therapy is expressed in:
questions.explanation: Dose (J/cm²) = power density (W/cm²) × time (s). Power is in watts, a rate of energy delivery (J/s).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Pleuritic chest pain is best described as:

options.A: A dull, central, band-like pain radiating to the jaw
options.B: A severe, sharp, stabbing pain, worse on inspiration, and not reproduced by palpation
options.C: A burning retrosternal pain worse when lying flat or bending forward
options.D: Pain that is only ever felt during exercise and never at rest

questions.explanation: Pleuritic chest pain, from inflammation of the parietal pleura, is classically a severe, sharp, stabbing pain that worsens on inspiration and is NOT reproduced by palpation — distinguishing it from musculoskeletal chest wall pain, which IS reproduced by palpation.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SH) typically results from rupture of which type of vascular lesion?

options.A: A saccular (berry) aneurysm affecting large blood vessels
options.C: Atherosclerotic plaque in the carotid artery only
options.D: Venous thrombosis in the dural sinuses exclusively

questions.explanation: Subarachnoid hemorrhage typically occurs from bleeding into the subarachnoid space, most often from rupture of a saccular (berry) aneurysm affecting the larger cerebral blood vessels, often related to congenital weakness in the vessel wall.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan, Physical Rehabilitation
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Low-dose aspirin helps prevent myocardial infarction and stroke primarily by:

options.A: Inhibiting thromboxane A2 formation, thereby preventing platelet aggregation

questions.explanation: Aspirin inhibits thromboxane A2 formation, which in turn prevents platelet aggregation — this is the physiological basis for using low-dose aspirin in the prevention of myocardial infarction and stroke.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.sourceChapter: Platelets or Thrombocytes — Functions, Important Note on Aspirin
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: The single most important variable in a programme designed to increase muscle strength is:
questions.explanation: Strength gains require a high intensity (70–85% of 1-RM) with low to moderate repetitions; endurance training uses low load and many repetitions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The correct sequence of wound healing phases is:
questions.explanation: Inflammatory (days 0–5), proliferative (days 4–21) and remodelling (21 days to 2 years).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: In a patient with a spinal cord injury who lacks active control of the back extensors, why might a therapist deliberately allow mild hypomobility to develop in the low back extensors while still fully stretching the hamstrings?

options.A: To create a stable, slightly shortened structure the patient can lean into for trunk support during long-term sitting
options.B: Because the back extensors cannot physically be stretched
options.C: To prevent contractures developing in the hamstrings only
options.D: Because stretching the trunk has no clinical value in this population

questions.explanation: This illustrates 'selective stretching': deliberately allowing some hypomobility in muscles the patient cannot actively control (like the back extensors after a thoracic/cervical spinal cord injury) gives them a stable structure to lean into for trunk stability while sitting, while the hamstrings are kept flexible enough for dressing and transfers.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 4: Stretching for Impaired Mobility — Selective Stretching
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Bilateral symmetrical pseudofractures (Looser's zones) are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Looser's zones are radiolucent bands perpendicular to the cortex.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Endometriosis is defined as the presence of:

options.B: Endometrial glands and stroma outside the uterine cavity
options.D: Excess endometrial thickness within the uterus

questions.explanation: Presents with dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia and subfertility; chocolate cysts in the ovaries.

questions.question: A full-thickness burn over the anterior neck is most likely to lead to a contracture in:
questions.explanation: Anterior neck scar shortens and pulls the neck into flexion; therapists must position the neck in extension without a pillow and use splints/collars.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
